To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found a large variation in Cd accumulation among 100 barley accessions and identified 9 major QTL for root Cd, shoot Cd, root-to-shoot Cd translocation and 2 major QTL for Cd accumulation in grain.

(i) there was a good correlation of the shoot Cd between solution and soil culture; (ii) there was no correlation of the root Cd and the grain Cd between solution and Cd contaminated soil culture; (iii) a common QTL for shoot Cd and root to shoot translocation was found on chromosome 5 H.
we identified a large genotypic variance in the Cd concentration in barley grain and different organs, and detected major QTL for Cd accumulation in barley.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic control of Cd accumulation of different barley organs, which provides a valuable reference for further understanding Cd accumulation in barley and other crops.
the identification of the QTL for Cd accumulation in the barley core collection, which is the first report of GWA analysis for grain Cd in barley.
the genetic control of the Cd accumulation in different barley organs and will contribute to the understanding of the mechanisms of Cd accumulation and translocation in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cd accumulation in barley is a polygenic trait controlled by many genes, and that the genetic architecture of Cd accumulation is different in different organs.
the QTL for Cd accumulation in grain is not necessarily the same as those for root and shoot Cd.
the genetic variation in Cd concentration in different organs and the QTL identified are useful for breeding low-Cd cultivars of barley.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variation in Cd concentrations of different organs is large and that the genetic control of Cd accumulation is complex.
there was a strong correlation between root and shoot Cd, and between shoot Cd and grain cadmium.

there is a good correlation between root Cd and shoot Cd, but not between root Cd and grain, and the major QTL identified for grain Cd are not the same as for shoot Cd and root Cd, indicating that grain Cd accumulation is a complex quantitative trait.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a good correlation between the shoot Cd in both hydroponic culture and Cd-contamined soil culture, and the root Cd and shoot Cd, but no significant correlation between the root and shoot Cd in the hydroponic culture.
the shoot Cd and the root-to-shoot Cd translocation are two key factors for grain Cd accumulation in barley.
